clue.text: Insect family with extensive members

parts.note: a father figure of the family whose limbs are very long: the crane fly with its spindly legs

explanation.surface: A naturalist describes a group of insects whose members are widespread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' means limbs, not people in a group, and 'extensive' means long; 'family' points to the head of the household. Together they describe the long-limbed crane fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly is commonly called by this name because of its very long, thin legs.

clue.text: Notice one model getting fat

parts.note: an advert is a notice, shortened to ad
the Roman numeral for one is I
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone spots that a fashion model has been putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose describes fatty tissue, so the adjective means fat or fatty.

clue.text: Squirrel's home moving three feet up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a yard is a length of three feet

explanation.surface: A squirrel relocates its nest a yard higher in the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' is surface colour; 'up' turns YARD round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirrel's nest is a drey, also spelt in this variant form.

clue.text: Reeling, a little drunk giving the glad eye

indicators.note: being slightly tipsy describes the letters of the word reeling staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy person sways about while making eyes at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the glad eye is to look at someone suggestively, which is what a lecherous look does.

clue.text: Pet with a connection — one from the old school?

parts.note: to pet is to kiss and cuddle, also called to neck
a tie is a link or connection

explanation.surface: Someone kissing and cuddling a fellow alumnus they share a bond with.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the 'old school tie', a neckwear item worn by former pupils of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: An old school tie is a piece of neckwear showing which school you went to.

clue.text: Celebrate when double comes up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: dual means double, twofold

explanation.surface: People celebrate when they roll a double at dice.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise highly, which is a way of celebrating someone.

clue.text: It's good to pay attention and look bright

parts.note: to listen is to pay attention to what is said

explanation.surface: Advice that paying attention in class makes you seem clever.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine or sparkle, so to look bright.

clue.text: Butt for the flower under the ha-ha

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another comes after it

parts.note: ha-ha is the sound of laughing
stock is a scented garden flower

explanation.surface: A gardener's flowers planted beneath a ha-ha, the sunken fence in a landscaped garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunk fence in British country gardens, which makes the surface horticultural; here it is just laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The butt of jokes is someone everyone laughs at, an object of ridicule.

clue.text: Getting compassionate

definitions.meaning: to get something is to grasp it, so getting means comprehension

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both comprehension of something and being sympathetic to others.

clue.text: Incite it in a football crowd

indicators.note: the word it goes in, inside the crowd

parts.note: the gate is the attendance at a football match

explanation.surface: A troublemaker stirs up the fans at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gate' is British usage for the number of spectators at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up or incite people to protest.

clue.text: Warning — it's a mock auction

indicators.note: a mock version is a false imitation, so the letters of auction are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beware: that sale is a sham auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A caution is a warning given to someone, as by police.

clue.text: Get a larger size

parts.note: reads like a shopping instruction to buy bigger clothes, but describes becoming bigger

explanation.surface: Advice in a shop to buy the next size up.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase in size is to expand or become bigger over time.

clue.text: Duplicator initially needs it to copy

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word duplicator is taken

explanation.surface: A copying machine requires the document fed into it to make a duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, a repetition of what came before.

clue.text: Pen note that the doctor should look at

definitions.text: that the doctor should look at

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: A written note about something a GP needs to examine.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid is something a GP might be asked to examine.

clue.text: Started to plead over article

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to beg is to plead earnestly
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone began begging for an item of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Began is the past tense of begin, a synonym of started.

clue.text: Speak for the whole people

definitions.meaning: to declare or say something formally
a nation or body politic considered as one

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for declaring and a noun for a nation or polity.

clue.text: A drifter of a coldly detached nature

definitions.text: A drifter of a coldly detached nature

parts.words: A drifter of a coldly detached nature
parts.note: sounds like an aloof vagrant, but describes a frozen mass broken from a glacier, floating at sea

explanation.surface: A description of an aloof, cold-hearted wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detached' means physically broken away from a glacier, and 'coldly' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating mass of frozen water drifts in the sea after breaking off a glacier.

clue.text: Nurse in bizarre sex case holds out

indicators.note: the jumbled letters form a case around the other piece
something bizarre is weird, so the letters of sex are rearranged

parts.note: to tend is to nurse or care for

explanation.surface: A nurse involved in a strange sex scandal stretches out a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre' turns SEX into EXS, which is the 'case' that holds TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend something is to hold it out or stretch it forward.

clue.text: I'm in favour yet show displeasure

indicators.note: the letters of I'm go inside the word for favour

parts.note: grace means favour, as in being in someone's good graces

explanation.surface: Someone claims to support a plan yet pulls a face.
explanation.definitionFit: To grimace is to twist the face to show disgust or disapproval.

clue.text: If a plan goes awry, you might be

definitions.text: If a plan goes awry, you might be

indicators.note: when things go wrong the letters of if a plan fall into a different order

explanation.surface: When your scheme fails you may end up flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agitated and panicky is the natural state when your scheme fails.

clue.text: Basic substance that's used in heating

definitions.meaning: a chemical substance that cannot be broken down further
the heating coil in a kettle or electric heater

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fundamental chemical constituent and a heating coil in an appliance.

clue.text: Atlantic liner docked next to a Queen

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: the Titanic was a famous Atlantic liner

explanation.surface: A transatlantic ship tied up beside a royal vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' looks like mooring, but means cutting off the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream she is the fairy queen.

clue.text: Attempts to reach high note somewhere in Italy

parts.note: tries are attempts
te is the seventh, highest note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer keeps trying to hit a top note at an Italian venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a port city in north-east Italy.

clue.text: Go on, Ann, develop a geometric figure

indicators.note: to develop something is to work it into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Encouraging Ann to work out a shape in a maths lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided polygon is a figure studied in geometry.

clue.text: Role reversal that can let an actor down

definitions.text: that can let an actor down

indicators.note: a reversal turns the word backwards

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: An actor being given an unsuitable role may flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let down' means disappoint in the surface but literally lower through the stage floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage trapdoor can lower a performer beneath the boards.

clue.text: Snail that goes round and round and up and down

definitions.meaning: a genus of land snails, including the garden snail

definitions.text: that goes round and round and up and down
definitions.meaning: describes a spiral shape like a corkscrew

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the snail genus name and also a three-dimensional spiral.

clue.text: Feedback for Miss Blyton?

parts.note: split feed-back: to feed is to dine, and back means read backwards, giving the children's author's first name

explanation.surface: Readers' comments sent to the children's author.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Feedback' as 'feed' (dine) read 'back'; Enid Blyton was a hugely popular British children's author.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid was the first name of the children's writer Blyton.

clue.text: Give players a hand

parts.note: sounds like applauding or helping performers, but means handing out cards

explanation.surface: Applaud the actors or help the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Distributing cards to each player at the table is the card-game sense.

clue.text: Accomplished fellow with a certain bearing

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
E is east, a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A capable man with a self-assured manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accomplished is finished or completed.

clue.text: Unusual glee shown after getting a pass in school

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: the letters of glee are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Unexpected delight after passing an exam to get into a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is a school, as in public schools like Eton College.

clue.text: Foreign Legion's drink

indicators.note: foreign means strange, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of legion plus its s

explanation.surface: What the French Foreign Legion drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A liqueur made by steeping blackthorn fruit in gin.

clue.text: Tip some runners? Tell us!

definitions.meaning: literally upset some runner pods out of a pot
an urge to reveal the secret

explanation.surface: A punter asks for racing tips and begs to be told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests horses and 'tip' a betting tip; really runner beans being tipped out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reveal a secret, and literally to spill legumes.
